high.title: Billion-Dollar Foreign Fund Managed by Dragon Capital Faces Redemption Pressure, May Be Forced to Sell Vietnamese Equities
high.summary: Vietnam Enterprise Investments Limited (VEIL), managed by Dragon Capital and one of the largest foreign funds active in Vietnamese equities, has completed a tender offer to buy back up to 10% of its outstanding shares. The result reveals significant redemption pressure: shareholders tendered a staggering 96.29 million shares — equivalent to 70.06% of total outstanding shares — far exceeding the 10% buyback cap. Of these, 72.99 million shares were tendered for cash and 23.30 million for an in-kind portfolio transfer. Due to the oversubscription, VEIL will apply a pro-rata allocation; excess tenders above basic entitlement will only be accepted at a 1.69% rate. The buyback price will be set at adjusted NAV as of July 8, 2026, less a 2.5% discount, with announcement expected on July 9.

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates on July 8 at Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
high.summary:
As Vietnam enters the second week of July 2026, the banking sector's deposit rate landscape remains broadly stable, with most institutions holding their online deposit rate schedules unchanged. The market continues to be tiered, with only a select group of banks posting rates at or above 7% per annum. ACB leads the market at 7.3% p.a. for 12-month tenors, also offering 7.2% for 9-month and 7.1% for 6-month deposits. Saigonbank follows at 7.2% for 12 months. MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB all post 7.0% for 12-month tenors, bringing the total number of banks at or above 7% for that tenor to six. The majority of the market clusters in the 6.6–6.9% range. **Implication for bond/FX traders:** The persistence of elevated deposit rates signals continued competition for liquidity among Vietnamese banks. Rates anchored above 7% at the upper end suggest the SBV has not yet pivoted decisively to an easing stance, which could weigh on government bond duration appetite and support VND stability by discouraging capital outflows into higher-yielding foreign assets. Watch for any coordinated rate reductions among state-owned banks (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank), which would signal a formal easing bias.

---

high.title: Government Approves ~VND 29,690 Billion Capital Injection for Agribank (2025–2027)
high.summary:
On July 6, 2026, Prime Minister issued Decision No. 1206/QĐ-TTg approving a phased capital injection of approximately VND 29,690 billion (~USD 1.16 billion) into Agribank — Vietnam's largest state-owned bank by assets — over the 2025–2027 period. The capital will be sourced from the central government budget as previously ratified by the National Assembly (Resolution 246/QH15). The injection is structured in two tranches: VND 9,525 billion in 2026 and VND 20,165 billion in 2027. Upon completion, Agribank's charter capital will rise significantly from VND 51,638 billion to VND 81,328 billion — a ~57% increase. As of June 30, 2026, total assets stood at over VND 2.7 quadrillion, with total mobilized capital exceeding VND 2.5 quadrillion. **For bond and equity investors:** This capital strengthening materially improves Agribank's CAR and lending capacity, supporting credit growth targets. It also signals continued government commitment to recapitalizing state-owned banks — a structural positive for the banking sector. Watch for potential Agribank bond issuance activity or changes to its lending rate as capital deployment accelerates.

---

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of July 7th at Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
high.summary:
The July 7th deposit rate snapshot reveals a continued bifurcation in Vietnam's banking system. Smaller banks maintain a clear competitive advantage in deposit pricing, while state-owned banks (SOEs) and large commercial banks hold rates steady. The top-tier payers include Saigonbank (leading at 7.2%/year for 12-month tenors, 7.0% for 18 months), MBV and VCBNeo (both at 7.0% across 6-, 9-, 12-, and 18-month tenors), PGBank (6.9–7.0% range), and VIB (7.0% for 12 months). A second cluster — LPBank, Bac A Bank, BVBank, and OCB — sits at 6.9% for 12-month deposits. **Market implications:** The persistence of 7%+ rates at smaller banks signals that liquidity competition remains elevated, putting upward pressure on lending rates and squeezing NIMs system-wide. For VND bond investors, elevated deposit rates at the short end of the curve act as a structural floor for short-tenor government bond yields. Watch for any convergence between small and large bank rates as a signal of improving system liquidity and a potential bond rally catalyst.

---

high.title: Three Foreign ETFs Hold Over $1.3 Billion in Vietnamese Equities: Fubon ETF Posts Best Performance Yet Faces Heaviest Outflows
high.summary:
Foreign capital outflows from Vietnamese equities have intensified in 2026, with net foreign selling on HoSE exceeding VND 82,000 billion year-to-date, extending a trend that began in 2025. Among the three largest foreign ETFs tracking Vietnam — VNM ETF, FTSE ETF, and Fubon ETF — outflow pressure has been significant. Fubon ETF has experienced the steepest redemptions, losing approximately TWD 2.6 billion (~USD 122 million) YTD, marking ten consecutive quarters of net outflows since mid-2023. Once seen as the flagship of Taiwanese capital flows into Vietnam when launched in 2021, Fubon's rapid growth has sharply reversed. VNM ETF recorded USD 26 million in net outflows YTD, its third consecutive year of redemptions. FTSE ETF bucked the trend with modest inflows of ~USD 2.6 million. **Key implications:** Persistent foreign selling creates structural headwinds for VND (via equity-related FX demand) and suppresses VN-Index sentiment. The sustained ETF outflow cycle suggests foreign institutional appetite for Vietnamese risk assets remains weak. Watch whether FTSE ETF's counter-trend inflow represents a rotation signal or is merely technical rebalancing.

---

medium.title: State Securities Commission of Vietnam (SSC) Signs MoUs with Two Major Universities to Strengthen Securities Industry Talent Development
medium.summary:
On July 8, 2026, the State Securities Commission of Vietnam (SSC) signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with the Foreign Trade University and the Academy of Finance. The agreements aim to enhance human capital quality for the securities and capital markets industry, promote academic research, and improve public financial literacy. The signing was attended by SSC Vice Chairman Nguyen Hoang Duong, along with representatives from the Vietnam Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation (VSDC), the Hanoi Stock Exchange, SSI Securities, and FiinGroup. While this is a structural/institutional development rather than a direct market-moving event, it signals the regulator's medium-term commitment to deepening Vietnam's capital markets. For international fund managers, a more professionally trained domestic investor and analyst base could support improved market microstructure, transparency, and liquidity on the VN-Index over time — a modest positive for long-term equity positioning in Vietnam.

---

medium.title: Global Gold Prices Sharply Reverse on Evening of July 8th
medium.summary:
Global gold prices dropped sharply on the evening of July 8, falling $140/oz to $4,040/oz, despite concurrent Middle East escalation including tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and Iran halting peace negotiations. The decline is attributed to investor positioning ahead of the release of the June FOMC meeting minutes, with the market reassessing the Fed's policy trajectory rather than reflexively fleeing to safe havens. The article notes a structural shift in safe-haven flows: geopolitical risk is now routing through crude oil and inflation expectations before reaching gold, rather than flowing directly into bullion.

**Relevance to Vietnam:** Domestic gold prices in Vietnam closely track global benchmarks, and sharp international moves can generate VND liquidity effects as local investors buy or sell gold. Additionally, Fed FOMC minutes may provide directional signals on USD strength, which directly impacts SBV's management of the VND/USD rate. A hawkish Fed read would put upward pressure on USD/VND and may require SBV intervention.

medium.title: Vietnam's Steel Exports Earn Over Half a Billion USD — Positive Signals from Russia and US Markets
medium.summary:
Vietnam's steel exports in May 2026 reached approximately 851,000 tonnes, generating $612 million in revenue. While export volume fell over 17% month-on-month, average export prices rose to $719/tonne — up nearly 9% from April and 7% year-on-year — indicating favorable pricing dynamics. For the first five months of 2026, cumulative steel exports totaled 4.7 million tonnes worth $3 billion USD, broadly flat in volume but slightly higher in value versus the same period in 2025. ASEAN remains the dominant destination, accounting for over 35% of exports ($1+ billion), supported by regional infrastructure investment activity.

**Relevance to Vietnam:** Steel export revenues contribute to Vietnam's trade surplus and support the current account balance, providing a natural source of USD inflows that underpin VND stability. Improving export unit prices, if sustained, could modestly strengthen Vietnam's external position and reduce pressure on SBV to defend the VND.

medium.title: SJC Gold and Plain-Band Gold Ring Prices on the Afternoon of July 8
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices in Vietnam continued to decline on the morning of July 8, falling VND 500,000–1.2 million per tael compared to the previous session — the third consecutive day of losses for both SJC gold bars and plain-band rings. SJC gold bars are now quoted at VND 146.5–149.5 million/tael, while plain-band rings stand at VND 146.2–149.2 million/tael. Internationally, spot gold pulled back to USD 4,127/oz after briefly recovering to USD 4,190/oz. Notably, the World Gold Council reported that central banks — including the People's Bank of China — used last month's price dip to accumulate reserves. For VND and FX watchers, domestic gold price dynamics matter as a proxy for unofficial USD demand and speculative pressure on the VND; easing gold prices reduce a key channel of informal FX outflows.

medium.title: Investors in Vietnam's Neighboring Country Suddenly Turn Away from Gold — Nearly $3 Billion Exits ETFs in One Month
medium.summary: According to the World Gold Council (WGC), June 2026 marked the largest ever monthly outflow from gold ETFs in China, with approximately USD 3 billion exiting Chinese mainland gold ETF products — the largest single such event on record. The primary driver was improving domestic risk appetite in China, as local equities rallied and the yuan strengthened, prompting investors to rotate from gold into higher-returning risk assets. Key funds affected include Huaan Yifu Gold ETF (-USD 1.14 billion), Guotai Gold ETF (-USD 352 million), and E Fund Gold ETF (-USD 334 million). This is a significant reversal from the first four months of 2026, when China was the world's top gold ETF inflow market. For Vietnamese markets, this is relevant as it reinforces the global gold price softening trend observed in Article 1, which can reduce speculative VND-to-gold conversion pressures and ease informal FX demand domestically.

medium.title: Statistics Since 2011 Reveal a Positive Signal for Vietnamese Stocks in July
medium.summary: In its latest strategy report, SSI Research notes that Vietnam's equity market enters July with more supportive factors than prior months, including the government's strong commitment to GDP growth targets (~11.9% for H2 2026), softening global oil prices, and expectations of continued corporate earnings improvement. However, SSI Research cautions that systemic liquidity conditions remain challenging: the gap between credit growth and deposit growth stays elevated, and persistent FX (VND) pressure is seen as a key constraint limiting the depth of any deposit rate cuts. As a result, SSI Research maintains a **sideways market** base case for July rather than a broad-based rally. For bond and FX traders, this is a notable signal — the acknowledgment that **VND exchange rate pressure is directly limiting monetary easing room** suggests the SBV faces a delicate balancing act. Accelerated public investment disbursement in H2 and a potential public sector wage increase could inject liquidity and support domestic consumption, but may also add inflationary pressure. Investors should monitor VND/USD dynamics closely as they remain a binding constraint on rate policy.

medium.title: BIDV to Pay Over VND 3,200 Billion in Cash Dividends — SBV as Majority Shareholder to Receive ~VND 2,600 Billion
medium.summary: BIDV's Board of Directors has approved a cash dividend payment for fiscal year 2025 at a rate of 4.5% of par value (VND 450/share), totaling over VND 3,276 billion (~USD 128 million). The ex-dividend date is July 17, with the record date July 20 and payment scheduled from August 20 onward. The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV), which holds a 79.56% stake in BIDV, is set to receive approximately VND 2,600 billion — a meaningful fiscal inflow for the regulator. Strategic foreign shareholder KEB Hana Bank (14.74%) will receive approximately VND 480 billion, representing an outbound capital flow in foreign currency terms that FX traders should note. This marks the second consecutive year BIDV has maintained a 4.5% cash dividend after years of stock-only distributions. While this is primarily a banking sector corporate action, the SBV's receipt of a large dividend from its listed bank subsidiary, and the associated FX outflow to KEB Hana Bank, carry marginal relevance for balance of payments and FX market monitoring.

medium.title: Not Interest Rates — This Is the Key Factor Determining VN-Index Direction Going Forward
medium.summary: BIDV Securities (BSC) released its H2 2026 strategy report, flagging that VN-Index gains remain heavily concentrated in a small number of large-cap stocks — most notably the Vingroup cluster. Excluding Vingroup stocks, the index would stand at approximately 1,742 points, down ~7% year-to-date, echoing a similar dynamic seen in 2025 when VN-Index rose 43% but only ~16% ex-Vingroup. BSC upgraded its 2026 corporate earnings forecast to VND 525,100 billion (+21.9% YoY; +3.7% vs. March estimates), noting quality improvement with 7 out of 19 industry groups recording core profit growth. For equity investors, the key takeaway is that broad market participation remains limited — index-level strength may be misleading, and stock selection is critical. The report suggests that earnings trajectory (not interest rates) will be the primary market driver in H2 2026.

medium.title: Vietnam's Largest Bank (BIDV) Prepares to Pay Cash Dividend and Announces Capital Increase Plan
medium.summary: BIDV's Board of Directors has approved a 4.5% cash dividend for 2025, with the record date set for July 20, 2026, and payment on August 20, 2026. Total cash outflow for dividends amounts to VND 3,276 billion (~USD 128 million at current rates). Separately, BIDV is executing a significant capital raise approved at its 2026 AGM, targeting a charter capital increase from the current level to approximately VND 100 trillion across 2026–2027. The first tranche — already approved by the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) in early June 2026 — involves issuing up to ~498 million new shares (6.84% ratio) to existing shareholders, raising charter capital from VND 72,800 billion to VND 77,782 billion. **Relevance:** BIDV's capital expansion is a key banking sector development; the SBV's approval of the share issuance signals regulatory comfort with major bank balance sheet growth. Equity investors should monitor dilution impact on BID's share price post-record date, while the large capital raise supports BIDV's capacity to extend credit and maintain system stability.

medium.title: Vietnamese Banks Expand Assets at Unprecedented Pace: One Bank Grew 12x in 10 Years; HDBank, MB, and TPBank Among Leaders
medium.summary: A decade-long review of 27 listed Vietnamese banks shows total system assets surged from VND 4.73 quadrillion at end-2015 to over VND 21.14 quadrillion by end-2025 — a 4.47x expansion, adding VND 16.41 quadrillion in balance sheet size. Structural transformation is equally notable: in 2015, only the Big 4 state banks had assets above VND 500 trillion; MB stood at just VND 221 trillion and VPBank/Techcombank hovered near VND 190 trillion. By end-2025, 13 banks had crossed the VND 500 trillion threshold, with the first institutions reaching VND 3 quadrillion. HDBank, MB, and TPBank are highlighted as top-tier growers. **Relevance for investors:** Rapid balance sheet expansion raises macro-prudential concerns around credit quality and capital adequacy that the SBV will need to manage. This structural growth also underpins strong demand for VND-denominated funding instruments including government bonds, and supports continued banking sector weight in the VN-Index.
